decisions.question: Renumber the page keys to follow the grouped page bar?
decisions.context: The page bar is now grouped into Play (Home, Mods, Tests, Logs, Memory, Game files, Atlas), Code (Changes, Timeline, Code map, Make-up) and Tools (Reports, Settings, Decisions). The keys still follow the old order: 1 Home, 2 Reports, 3 Atlas, 4 Tests, 5 Mods, 6 Changes, 7 Timeline, 8 Code map, 9 Settings, G Logs, M Make-up, D Decisions. Memory (U) and Game files (W) keep their letters either way.

options.label: Renumber them
options.detail: 1 Home, 2 Mods, 3 Tests, 4 Logs, 5 Atlas, 6 Changes, 7 Timeline, 8 Code map, 9 Make-up; E Reports, S Settings, D Decisions. G and M are freed. Keys you changed yourself stay as you set them

options.label: Keep them as they are
options.detail: No key changes; the numbers no longer match the bar's order

decisions.why: The number keys would count along the bar you see; they are a day old, so little is lost in learning them again

decisions.question: Should agents in every repository put the choices they make for you on this page?
decisions.context: Today only the Companion's own agent choices are here. As a shared rule, every repository (phobos-rimworld and the rest) would list its agent choices and open questions in its own config/decisions.json, and this page would gather them all.

options.label: Yes, every repository
options.detail: A shared rule in phobos-modkit's rules; design records still label choices as now

options.label: Only the Companion's
options.detail: Other repositories keep their choices in their design records

decisions.why: Choices scattered across design records are easy to miss; one page with buttons is the point of this page

decisions.question: Are the page sizes right for how far back you read?
decisions.context: Ten days a page on the Timeline, six versions a page on Changes, 25 test rows on Tests, 20 kinds of message on Logs, eight backups a page on Mods, ten commits a page in a thing's history.

options.label: Show more on each page
options.detail: About twice as many: fewer page turns, longer pages

options.label: Show fewer on each page
options.detail: About half: shorter pages, more turns

decisions.why: Each was chosen to fit one screen on your monitor; change them if a page feels cut short

decisions.question: When should the Code map ring a patched method in red?
decisions.context: A method our code patches gets a red dotted ring when three or more other mods patch it too, or the last update changed it.

options.label: Three or more other mods (as now)
Two or more
options.detail: More rings: earlier warning, more noise

options.label: Five or more
options.detail: Fewer rings: only the busiest methods

decisions.why: On your mod list, three marked the methods where clashes have actually happened

decisions.question: How quickly should the activity strip appear under the page bar?
decisions.context: The strip shows anything the window is waiting on. Work that finishes within 0.6 seconds never shows it.

options.label: After 1.5 seconds
options.detail: Only work you would notice waiting for

options.label: Always
options.detail: Every request flickers it, however quick

decisions.why: Quick reads stay quiet, and anything you would wait on says so

decisions.question: How far back should Make-up count recent changes?
decisions.context: Make-up's 'how often it changed' colouring and the Code map's busiest code count the last 30 days.

options.label: 7 days
options.detail: What this week's work touched

options.label: 90 days
options.detail: Where the work has gone this season

decisions.why: Long enough to see where work keeps returning, short enough that last month's rework fades

decisions.question: Build the last two cross-links: design records joined to code (S1) and rules joined to the checks that enforce them (S5)?
decisions.context: Both are in docs/cross-links.md and docs/later.md. S1 would show, beside a design record's section, the code that builds it; S5, beside each rule, the check that holds it.

options.label: After the game-files work
options.detail: Saves, screenshots and what changed since you last played come first

decisions.why: The game-files views are more use day to day; S1 and S5 serve agents more than you

decisions.question: Add 'Size as installed' to Make-up?
decisions.context: Make-up measures lines, size in the repository and files. Size as installed would measure what each mod takes in the game's Mods folder, encoded textures included.
decisions.why: Textures make installed size very different from repository size, and the install records already know where each mod is

decisions.question: May the Companion offer to delete old autosaves and Real Ruins files to free space?
decisions.context: RimWorld's saves folder holds 15 GB (46 files) and Real Ruins 1.5 GB in 16,231 files. Today the Companion would only show sizes.

options.label: Sizes only
options.detail: It shows what takes the space; you delete by hand

options.label: Offer, and ask every time
options.detail: A button lists exactly what would go and waits for your yes; never your named saves, only autosaves and caches

decisions.why: Saves are the one thing that cannot be rebuilt; this is yours to choose, not mine

decisions.question: Make the Companion run on another computer, or for someone else?
decisions.context: Today it finds the tool kit by the folder it was built from and needs Python on the PATH, so it cannot be handed to anyone.
decisions.why: Nothing needs it yet, and it is easiest once the pages settle

decisions.question: Is ! (Shift+1) the right key for Something's off?
decisions.context: One key on any page draws the page and asks what looks wrong, for the next agent session.
decisions.why: An exclamation is what you would say on seeing it; any key can still be changed under Settings

decisions.question: How old may the newest records copy get before Home speaks up?
decisions.context: Home shows a note when the Companion's records have never been copied, or the newest copy is this old.
decisions.why: A week of verdicts is the most you would want to lose, and a weekly nudge is not nagging

decisions.question: When should a session's claim be marked old?
decisions.context: The claims board marks a claim old after a day: perhaps a session that ended without letting go.
decisions.why: Batches run over an evening; a claim older than a day is almost always forgotten

decisions.question: Mark a moment in a memory watch without leaving the game?
decisions.context: Today a mark needs the Companion in front: Alt+Tab, B, a few words, Enter, then back to the game. The page's own keys are one key each, but a key that works while the game is in front has to be two held together, or the game would lose that key. It needs a new library (Tauri's global shortcut plugin).

options.label: Add a key that works in the game
options.detail: Ctrl+Alt+M (changeable) marks the moment at once as 'marked from the game', without leaving the game; add words on the Memory page afterwards

options.label: Keep marks in the Companion's window
options.detail: Alt+Tab, B, words, Enter, as now

decisions.why: Switching windows mid-reload is the moment marks matter most and the moment you are least free to type; one press keeps the time exact and spares the mouse

decisions.question: Start a memory watch by itself when the game starts?
decisions.context: You restart the game often, and a watch ends when the game closes. The Companion could notice the game starting and begin a watch for you. With .NET's figures that attaches to the game each time without asking; Windows' figures only attaches nothing.

options.label: Only when I press Start
options.detail: As now: every watch asks first

options.label: By itself, Windows' figures only
options.detail: Attaches nothing; every session gets a watch, without .NET's split

options.label: By itself, with .NET's figures
options.detail: Attaches once each time the game starts, without asking

decisions.why: Every watch so far was read against a plan (what to do, when to reload); a watch nobody planned is hard to read. Change it if you find yourself forgetting to start one

decisions.question: Is 15 minutes the right first choice for a memory watch?
decisions.context: The page offers 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 and 60 minutes, with 15 chosen to begin with. You found 60 a bit generous and 15 to 20 workable, and you reload every 10 to 15 minutes.

options.label: 15 minutes (as now)
options.detail: About one reload's worth

options.label: 20 minutes
options.detail: Room for a reload and a few minutes after it

options.label: 10 minutes
options.detail: Shorter, for quick checks

decisions.why: It fits between your reloads; the other lengths are one press away

decisions.question: Are U, T, B and X the right keys for the Memory page?
decisions.context: U opens the page from anywhere; on the page, T starts a watch (it asks first), B starts a mark and X stops the running watch. S was left free because the page-keys question would give it to Settings.

options.label: Keep them
options.detail: Any key can still be changed in Settings, Keyboard shortcuts

options.label: Change them
options.detail: Say which in your words

decisions.why: B (bookmark) and X (stop) are easy to find without looking; the rest were what was free

decisions.question: Teach the Code map to read TypeScript, Svelte and Rust, so the tools entry's own code can be followed?
decisions.context: 0.24.0 lists your tools (the Companion, the kit and the logger) beside your games. The Code map reads C#, XML Defs, Lua and Python, so it follows the kit's Python but not the Companion's Svelte, TypeScript or Rust: for phobos-companion it says nothing was read. Ostranauts and RimWorld are C#; none of your games' mods use these three.

options.label: All three
options.detail: New readers in the kit for TypeScript, Svelte and Rust: calls, imports, components and Tauri commands joined window to host

options.label: TypeScript and Svelte first
options.detail: The window's code; Rust after

options.label: Later
options.detail: Leave the Code map to your games' languages for now

decisions.why: The join that matters most is a window request to the host command that answers it, and that needs both sides read

decisions.question: How much of decompiling should the Companion take on?
decisions.context: Today agents decompile through the kit (query-code, assembly-archive compare, ilspycmd set in central settings) and the results stay in each repository's .local or the kit's cache. The Code map reads only your own repositories. Other authors' code you meet there (a Harmony patch's target, a VF method) is a dead end on screen.

options.label: Read and compare, on your press
options.detail: Code map follows a patch into the other author's method: public source first, an existing decompile second, and a Decompile button (with its bar) when neither is there. A 'What did this update change?' view over the assembly archive. Read-only, per game through the kit, so .NET games (RimWorld, Ostranauts) and Java (Project Zomboid's classes) can each bring their own decompiler

options.label: Only what an update changed
options.detail: The archive's member-by-member compare on a page; no browsing of other authors' code

options.label: Leave it to agents
options.detail: The Companion shows our code only

decisions.why: The patch-to-target jump and the update compare are the two questions you ask most when something breaks after an update; the kit already does the work, the Companion would only show it
